args.summary:
Decision: PROMOTE canary 1.1, written to review/C-evidence-2/decision.json.

Evidence (all from run_query over the raw request log, 9785 rows: 7374 stable / 2411 canary):
1. No error regression - every request on both versions returned 200; non-200 = 0 and 5xx = 0 for v1.0 and v1.1.
2. No latency regression - aggregate and per-path percentiles match within 1 ms: ALL p50 34/34, p95 94/93, p99 104/105; /browse p50 22/22 p95 27/27; /search p50 47/47 p95 59/59; /checkout p50 81/82 p95 103/104. Max absolute delta across all those comparisons = 1 ms.
3. Stability over time - in all four 30 s windows the canary-vs-stable p95 gap is <= 4 ms (2, 2, 2, 4 ms) with 0 5xx in every window; the 90-120 s window shows canary p95 96 vs stable 92, i.e. no worsening trend beyond noise.
4. The one asymmetry found, labelled as such: /browse requests slower than 40 ms occur at 1.08% on canary (13/1200) vs 0.41% on stable (15/3672), two-proportion z ~ 2.7 (expected 6.9 at the pooled 0.57% rate vs 13 observed). Judgement: this is not promote-blocking because the tail is bounded at the same ceiling as stable (canary /browse max 87 ms = stable /browse max 87 ms, both below the service-wide stable p95 of 94 ms), the 13 events are spread evenly across the 120 s (2s..115s) rather than clustered, and the effect is invisible at /browse p95 (27 ms on both). It is small-n on 1200 requests and worth watching after promote.

Judgement call: promote, with the /browse slow-tail rate as the metric to watch at 100% traffic.
